passages.text: The following combined discussion and analysis should be read in combination with the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 herein. The discussion of CenterPoint Energy’s consolidated financial information includes the results of CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, LLC and CenterPoint Energy Resources Corp., which, along with CenterPoint Energy, Inc., are collectively referred to as the Registrants. Where appropriate, information relating to a specific Registrant has been segregated and labeled as such. Unless the context indicates otherwise, specific references to Houston Electric and CERC also pertain to CenterPoint Energy. In this combined Form 10-K, the terms “our,” “we” and “us” are used as abbreviated references to CenterPoint Energy, Inc. together with its consolidated subsidiaries, including Houston Electric and CERC, unless otherwise stated. No Registrant makes any representation as to the information relating to the other Registrants or the subsidiaries of CenterPoint Energy, Inc. other than itself or its subsidiaries. OVERVIEW Background CenterPoint Energy is a public utility holding company. CenterPoint Energy’s operating subsidiaries own and operate electric transmission, distribution and generation facilities and natural gas distribution systems. For a detailed description of CenterPoint Energy’s operating subsidiaries, see Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements. Houston Electric is an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of CenterPoint Energy, which provides electric transmission service to transmission service customers in the ERCOT region and distribution service to REPs serving the Texas Gulf Coast area that includes the city of Houston. 50 CERC Corp. is an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of CenterPoint Energy, which (i) directly owns and operates natural gas distribution systems in Minnesota and Texas, (ii) indirectly, through Indiana Gas and CEOH, owns and operates natural gas distribution systems in Indiana and Ohio, respectively, and (iii) owns and operates permanent pipeline connections through interconnects with various interstate and intrastate pipeline companies through CEIP. On October 20, 2025, CenterPoint Energy, through its subsidiary CERC Corp., entered into the Ohio Securities Purchase Agreement to sell all of the issued and outstanding equity interests in CEOH. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. For further information, see Note 4 to the consolidated financial statements. Reportable Segments We discuss our operating results on a consolidated basis and individually for each of our reportable segments. We are first and foremost an energy delivery company and it is our intention to remain focused on these regulated segments. The results of our business operations are significantly impacted by weather, customer growth, economic conditions, cost management, competition, rate proceedings before regulatory agencies and other actions of the various regulatory agencies to whose jurisdiction we are subject, among other factors. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: CenterPoint Energy is a holding company that conducts all of its business operations through subsidiaries, primarily Houston Electric, CERC and SIGECO. The following, along with any additional legal proceedings identified or incorporated by reference in Item 3 of this combined report on Form 10-K, summarizes the principal risk factors associated with the holding company and the businesses conducted by its subsidiaries. However, additional risks and uncertainties either not presently known or not currently believed by management to be material may also adversely affect CenterPoint Energy’s businesses. For other factors that may cause actual results to differ from those indicated in any forward-looking statement or projection contained in this combined report on Form 10-K, see “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Certain Factors Affecting Future Earnings” in Item 7, which should be read in conjunction with the risk factors contained in this Item 1A. Carefully consider each of the risks described below, including those relating to Houston Electric, LLC and CenterPoint Energy Resources Corp., which, along with CenterPoint Energy, Inc., are collectively referred to as the Registrants. Unless the context indicates otherwise, where appropriate, information relating to a specific Registrant has been segregated and labeled as such and specific references to Houston Electric and CERC in this section also pertain to CenterPoint Energy. In this combined report on Form 10-K, the terms “our,” “we” and “us” are used as abbreviated references to CenterPoint Energy, Inc. together with its consolidated subsidiaries. Risk Factors Affecting Operations Electric Transmission, Distribution and Generation (CenterPoint Energy and Houston Electric) Disruptions at third-party or Indiana Electric’s power generation facilities, generation inadequacy, directives issued by regulatory authorities or other matters could cause interruptions in Houston Electric’s and Indiana Electric’s ability to provide transmission and distribution services and Houston Electric and Indiana Electric may not be able to promptly respond, repair and restart their facilities, which could adversely affect their businesses, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Houston Electric owns the transmission and distribution infrastructure in its service territory that delivers electric power to its customers, but it does not own or operate any bulk power generation facilities. Indiana Electric owns and operates power generation facilities in addition to the transmission and distribution infrastructure in its service territory. Both Houston Electric and Indiana Electric must follow the directives issued by their independent system operator, ERCOT and MISO, respectively. ERCOT and MISO have in the past and may in the future issue directives requiring members to implement controlled outages as a result of an emergency or reliability issues. credit_strengths.text: CenterPoint Energy's regulated electric and gas delivery operations generate stable, recurring revenue, with operating income rising over the past three fiscal years. The operating margin remains solid, though it sits modestly below the utilities sector median, reflecting the capital-intensive nature of transmission and distribution assets and the company's ongoing investment program.

Operating cash flow has recovered from the prior-year trough and covers interest expense comfortably, with interest coverage modestly below the sector median but still adequate for an investment-grade utility. The company's scale and essential-service demand provide a durable foundation for debt service.

key_risks.text: CenterPoint Energy is a holding company conducting all operations through subsidiaries, primarily Houston Electric and CERC. This structural subordination means parent-level creditors rely on subsidiary dividends, which may be restricted by regulatory capital requirements or debt covenants, potentially limiting cash available for parent debt service.

The company's debt burden has grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, with gross leverage well above the utilities sector median and net leverage similarly elevated. This highly leveraged profile leaves limited headroom, and a modest EBITDA decline could pressure credit metrics further.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow is deeply negative, as capital expenditures substantially exceed operating cash flow, and the company also pays common dividends. This means debt service depends on continued access to external financing, and the negative FCF-to-debt ratio underscores the reliance on capital markets.

The current ratio is below one, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets, and cash on hand is minimal relative to debt. While utilities often operate with negative working capital, the combination of high leverage and thin liquidity amplifies refinancing risk if market conditions tighten.

overall_credit_view.text: CenterPoint Energy's credit profile is highly leveraged, with net leverage above the utilities sector median and an indicative financial risk profile of 'Highly leveraged'. The company's regulated operations provide stable cash flow, but weak free cash flow generation and high debt constrain financial flexibility.

Our forward-looking view is that leverage will remain elevated given the company's capital program and dividend commitments. While the sale of CEOH may provide some debt reduction, the overall credit trajectory depends on regulatory outcomes and management's ability to fund growth without further straining the balance sheet.

credit_strengths.text: CenterPoint Energy 的受規管電力及燃氣輸配業務產生穩定、經常性收入，過去三個財政年度的經營收入持續上升。經營利潤率維持穩健，惟略低於公用事業行業中位數，反映輸電及配電資產屬資本密集型，以及公司持續的投資計劃。
經營現金流已從上一年度的低谷回升，並能從容覆蓋利息支出，利息覆蓋率略低於行業中位數，但對投資級公用事業而言仍屬足夠。公司的規模及基本服務需求為償債提供穩固基礎。

key_risks.text: CenterPoint Energy 為控股公司，所有業務均透過附屬公司進行，主要為 Houston Electric 及 CERC。此結構性次級關係意味著母公司層面的債權人依賴附屬公司派發股息，而該等股息可能受監管資本要求或債務契約限制，或會限制可用於母公司償債的現金。
公司債務負擔於過去三個財政年度穩步增加，總槓桿遠高於公用事業行業中位數，淨槓桿亦同樣高企。此高度槓桿的狀況令緩衝空間有限，EBITDA 若溫和下降，或會進一步對信用指標構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流嚴重為負，因資本開支大幅超過經營現金流，且公司亦派發普通股股息。這意味著償債依賴持續取得外部融資，而負值的 FCF 對債務比率凸顯其對資本市場的依賴。
流動比率低於一，顯示流動負債超過流動資產，且手頭現金相對債務而言極少。儘管公用事業常以負營運資金運作，但高槓桿與流動性薄弱並存，若市場環境收緊，將放大再融資風險。

overall_credit_view.text: CenterPoint Energy 的信用狀況高度槓桿，淨槓桿高於公用事業行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為「高度槓桿」。公司的受規管業務提供穩定現金流，但自由現金流產生疲弱及高債務限制財務靈活性。
我們的前瞻性觀點是，鑑於公司的資本計劃及股息承諾，槓桿將維持高企。儘管出售 CEOH 或可帶來部分債務削減，整體信用軌跡取決於監管結果及管理層在不進一步繃緊資產負債表的情況下為增長提供資金的能力。
